 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx161829_1"></A>ITEM&nbsp;5.02 DEPARTURE OF DIRECTORS OR CERTAIN OFFICERS; ELECTION OF
DIRECTORS; APPOINTMENT OF CERTAIN OFFICERS; COMPENSATORY ARRANGEMENTS OF CERTAIN OFFICERS </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On March&nbsp;10, 2011 General
Motors Company (&#147;GM&#148;) issued a news release announcing that Christopher P. Liddell had resigned from his position as Vice Chairman and Chief Financial Officer of General Motors Company. Mr.&nbsp;Liddell&#146;s resignation will be effective
April&nbsp;1, 2011. Mr.&nbsp;Liddell informed GM of his decision on March&nbsp;7, 2010. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GM also announced that Daniel Ammann
has been appointed Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer effective April&nbsp;1, 2011. Mr.&nbsp;Ammann, 38, was named GM Vice President, Finance and Treasurer of General Motors Company in April 2010. Before joining GM, he was Managing
Director and Head of Industrial Investment Banking for Morgan Stanley, a position he held since 2004. During his 11 years at Morgan Stanley, he was responsible for many significant assignments spanning a variety of technology, service, and
manufacturing clients, including advising General Motors Corporation during its restructuring and sale of assets to GM. Mr.&nbsp;Ammann has no other reportable relationships with GM or its affiliates. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Mr.&nbsp;Ammann&#146;s compensation in his new position has not yet been determined. GM will file a Current Report on Form 8-K to report
his compensation arrangements when they have been agreed upon. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx161829_2"></A>ITEM&nbsp;9.01 FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND EXHIBITS
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><U>EXHIBITS </U></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

<DESCRIPTION>NEWS RELEASE
<TEXT>
<HTML><HEAD>
<TITLE>News Release</TITLE>
</HEAD>
 <BODY BGCOLOR="WHITE">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="right"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx161829_4"></A>Exhibit 99.1 </B></FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center">

<IMG SRC="g161829ex991-pg001.jpg" ALT="LOGO"> </P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For Release: 8:15 AM EST </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">March&nbsp;10, 2011 </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:24px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>GM Announces CFO Transition </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="9%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Chris Liddell Steps Down After Record IPO</B> </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="9%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Treasurer Dan Ammann to assume CFO Role</B> </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>DETROIT</B> &#150; General Motors Vice Chairman and Chief Financial Officer Chris Liddell today announced that he will leave the company April&nbsp;1, 2011, having completed the largest public offering
in history and stabilizing the company&#146;s financial operations. Liddell, 52, joined GM in January, 2010 and led the company&#146;s financial and accounting operations on a global basis. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#147;Chris was a major contributor during a pivotal time in the company&#146;s history,&#148; said Dan Akerson, GM chairman and CEO. &#147;He guided the company&#146;s IPO process and established a good
financial foundation for the future.&#148; </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition to the successful IPO, Akerson recognized Liddell&#146;s leadership over the last year
noting four quarters of sustained profitability, a strengthened balance sheet and the elimination of material weakness in the financial reporting process. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Dan Ammann will succeed Liddell as General Motors chief financial officer, effective April&nbsp;1, 2011. Ammann, 38, is currently GM vice president, finance and treasurer. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#147;Dan&#146;s depth of knowledge of the financial community and our business will be instrumental as we continue to earn the trust of global investors
and customers,&#148; said Akerson. &#147;He is held in high regard on Wall Street and within the company and, as we move our financial strategy forward, his credibility and leadership will be invaluable.&#148; </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Ammann has played a major role in the key financial decisions at the new GM. He has been actively engaged in setting the financial strategy and reducing
debt. Ammann was also integral in the IPO process. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#147;We&#146;ve made great strides this last year in setting the financial strategy for
the company,&#148; said Ammann. &#147;Chris and I have worked together very closely during this time and I am committed to a seamless transition and to building on what we started.&#148; </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Since joining the company in March, 2010, Ammann has led the GM Treasurer&#146;s Office, based in New York, with operations around the world. Prior to GM, Ammann was managing director and head of
Industrials Investment Banking for Morgan Stanley and was instrumental in many high profile assignments spanning a variety of technology, service, and manufacturing clients. </FONT></P>

<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#147;I came to General Motors to be part of something great,&#148; said Liddell. &#147;My objective was to
help rebuild this iconic company and I am particularly pleased that through this process, we have also developed a strong successor in Dan Ammann.&#148; </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A successor for Ammann in GM&#146;s Treasurer&#146;s Office will be announced at a later date. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">### </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>About General Motors:</B> General Motors, one of the world&#146;s largest automakers,
traces its roots back to 1908. With its global headquarters in Detroit, GM employs 202,000 people in every major region of the world and does business in more than 120 countries. GM and its strategic partners produce cars and trucks in 30 countries,
and sell and service these vehicles through the following brands: Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, FAW, GMC, Daewoo, Holden, Jiefang, Opel, Vauxhall and Wuling. GM&#146;s largest national market is China, followed by the United States, Brazil, Germany,
the United Kingdom, Canada, and Italy. GM&#146;s OnStar subsidiary is the industry leader in vehicle safety, security and information services. More information on the new General Motors can be found at www.gm.com. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Forward-Looking Statements: </B>In this press release and in related comments by our management, our use of the words &#147;expect,&#148;
&#147;anticipate,&#148; &#147;possible,&#148; &#147;potential,&#148; &#147;target,&#148; &#147;believe,&#148; &#147;commit,&#148; &#147;intend,&#148; &#147;continue,&#148; &#147;may,&#148; &#147;would,&#148; &#147;could,&#148; &#147;should,&#148;
&#147;project,&#148; &#147;projected,&#148; &#147;positioned&#148; or similar expressions is intended to identify forward-looking statements that represent our current judgment about possible future events. We believe these judgments are reasonable,
but these statements are not guarantees of any events or financial results, and our actual results may differ materially due to a variety of important factors. Among other items, such factors might include: our ability to realize production
efficiencies and to achieve reductions in costs as a result of our restructuring initiatives and labor modifications; our ability to maintain quality control over our vehicles and avoid material vehicle recalls; our ability to maintain adequate
liquidity and financing sources and an appropriate level of debt, including as required to fund our planning significant investment in new technology; our ability to realize successful vehicle applications of new technology; and our ability to
continue to attract new customers, particularly for our new products. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GM&#146;s most recent annual report on Form 10-K and quarterly report
on Form 10-Q provides information about these and other factors, which we may revise or supplement in future reports to the SEC. </FONT></P>
